ai.title: load-agents skips skills directory during recursive agent scan
ai.summary: load-agents.ts adds a guard to skip directories named 'skills' during recursive agent file discovery. This prevents agent loading logic from scanning skill-specific files, isolating agent definitions from skill implementations. Scope limited to sdk/src/agents/load-agents.ts.

eli5.text: When the system looks through folders to find available helpers, it now skips any folder named 'skills' so those files aren't treated as helper definitions. This only affects how the system organizes helper files internally, and you won't notice anything different unless you're specifically managing those files. The change is live today.

ai.title: Add credits per dollar tooltip to pricing tiers
ai.summary: Added a `HelpCircle` tooltip to `pricing-client.tsx` displaying calculated credits per dollar for each subscription tier. The `CREDITS_PER_DOLLAR` constant derives values from `SUBSCRIPTION_TIERS` using a fixed `WEEKS_PER_MONTH` multiplier. Users see exact value metrics on hover in the Web pricing UI.

eli5.text: When you look at the pricing page and hover your mouse over the small question-mark icon next to a plan, a small box pops up showing how many credits you get for each dollar spent on that plan. This helps you quickly compare which subscription gives you better value. The tool that analyzes code changes rated this as a very minor update, meaning it's a small addition rather than a major overhaul.

ai.title: Include subscription credits in API balance checks
ai.summary: Web endpoints now include subscription credits in balance calculations when `ensureSubscriberBlockGrant` is provided. `calculateUsageAndBalance` accepts an `includeSubscriptionCredits` flag to bypass the `isPersonalContext` exclusion for subscription grants. This ensures newly created block grants are immediately visible to the credit gating logic in `checkCreditsAndCharge` and `postChatCompletions`. Covers `web/src/app/api/v1` and `packages/billing`.

eli5.text: The system now checks your subscription credits (like a prepaid block of usage) at the same time it checks your regular balance when you make an API call, so those credits are counted toward what you can do right away instead of only showing up separately. Previously, freshly created subscription grants could be invisible to the credit-check step, meaning a newly created block grant wouldn't be recognized until later. If you use the chat completions or web search/docs search endpoints, any eligible subscription block grant is now created and applied during the same request instead of being delayed.

ai.title: Add applypatch tool, Codex agents, thinking UI tweak
ai.summary: Added `apply_patch` tool for file operations (create, update, delete) using Codex-style diff format across SDK, agent runtime, and CLI. New `thinker-codex` and `code-reviewer-codex` agents use `openai/gpt-5.3-codex`. CLI thinking component now suppresses rendering for short single-bold messages. `base-deep` agent added with orchestration prompts.

eli5.text: Developers can now use a new tool that lets the assistant create, update, or delete files using a simple text format similar to a set of instructions. This works across the main assistant software, the developer tools they build with, and the command-line app. You'd notice this if you're building or testing the software and want to manage project files more efficiently, especially with the new model-powered assistants that understand this file-editing style.

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 1.0.622 ships with OpenRouter Claude Sonnet 4.6 mapping
ai.summary: Version 1.0.622 is a release-bump rollup of user-facing work from 2026-02-25 through 2026-02-26. It maps anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6 to the Anthropic model identifier in the OpenRouter adapter found in common/src/constants/claude-oauth.ts, adds an Account tab to the web profile page via a new AccountSection component, and introduces the apply_patch file tool across the SDK, agent runtime, and CLI using a Codex-style diff format. Additional notable changes include a credits-per-dollar tooltip on the Web pricing tiers, a confirmation dialog guarding the auto top-up feature against accidental charges, and reordering of the completions API credit check after subscription block grant validation so subscribers are no longer blocked by a-la-carte 402 responses. The Codex-style tool ships alongside new thinker-codex and code-reviewer-codex agents based on openai/gpt-5.3-codex, while the CLI thinking component suppresses short single-bold message rendering.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies a single line in cli/release/package.json, incrementing the version field from 1.0.621 to 1.0.622, as confirmed by the release-bump commit nature and the version 1.0.622 noted in the analysis notes.

eli5.text: This release brings smoother model access, clearer account controls, and smarter safety checks to the Freebuff experience. The platform now correctly recognizes and routes requests for the newest Claude Sonnet 4.6 model through OpenRouter, so you get the latest AI capabilities without manual configuration. A new Account tab on your web profile lets you view your email and verification status in one place, and the Discord bot now tells you exactly which email GitHub needs to connect your account. Auto top-ups now ask you to confirm before charging when your balance is low, preventing surprise bills, and pricing pages now show a tooltip explaining how many credits you get per dollar spent. Subscription credits now count toward your balance checks, so paid subscribers can keep working even when their separate credit pool runs low. Finally, new file-editing tools and Codex-style agents improve how the AI reads and updates your projects, with a cleaner thinking display that stays out of the way for quick notes.

ai.title: Switch buffbench eval agent from base2-free to base-deep
ai.summary: Eval runner in evals/buffbench/main.ts now targets 'base-deep' instead of 'base2-free'. Change aligns benchmark execution with deep agent variant. Scope limited to Evals subsystem.

eli5.text: The benchmark test that measures how well certain assistants perform has been switched to use a different assistant variant called 'base-deep' instead of 'base2-free'. This only affects internal developers running these evaluation tests; regular users won't notice any difference. If you run the benchmark today, it will test the 'base-deep' configuration rather than the previous 'base2-free' one.
